questions.q: How does a switch learn which port a device is connected to?
options: By reading the source MAC address of incoming frames
By reading the destination IP address of packets
By reading the port number in the TCP header
questions.explain: A switch records the source MAC address of every frame together with the port it arrived on.

questions.q: What does a switch do with a frame whose destination MAC address is not in its MAC address table?
options: Sends it back to the sender
Floods it out of every port except the one it arrived on
Sends it to the router only
questions.explain: Unknown unicast frames are flooded. When the destination replies, the switch learns its port.

options: A faster type of Ethernet cable
A logical grouping of devices into a separate broadcast domain on the same physical switch
questions.explain: VLANs split one physical switch into several logical networks, each with its own broadcast domain.

questions.q: Which command places an access port into VLAN 10?
questions.explain: Use switchport mode access and then switchport access vlan 10 in interface configuration mode.

questions.q: What is needed for devices in different VLANs to communicate?
options: A router or a Layer 3 switch
questions.explain: Different VLANs are different networks, so traffic between them must be routed.

questions.q: What does a trunk port carry?
options: Traffic for several VLANs, identified by 802.1Q tags
questions.explain: A trunk carries many VLANs over one link, and 802.1Q tags show which VLAN each frame belongs to.

questions.q: How many bits does the VLAN ID in an 802.1Q tag have?
questions.explain: 12 bits allow VLAN IDs from 0 to 4095, and VLANs 1 to 4094 are usable.

options: It uses one router interface per VLAN
It uses one physical interface divided into subinterfaces, one per VLAN
It removes VLANs from the switch
It uses a hub between the VLANs
questions.explain: A single trunk link to the router is divided into subinterfaces, and each one is the gateway of one VLAN.
